considerations: The first loader audio URL has a trailing ASCII space. Trim outer whitespace before URL encoding; encoding that trailing space as %20 would address a different object.
Three audio filenames have interior spaces. catalogue.json audio_url percent-encodes path spaces; audio_url_source preserves exact loader values.
Thirteen audio filenames end in .wav and fifteen in .mp3. The extensions do not verify actual codec/container or browser support; response headers and audio metadata need validation.

Two image filenames end in .heic. SSR uses Shopify resized/cropped CDN URLs, which may negotiate a browser-compatible response. Verify response Content-Type and decoding rather than assuming the filename extension is the transmitted format.

Seeking/duration depend on audio metadata and server response. Check a small Range: bytes=0-1023 request for 206/Content-Range without downloading a full mix, together with Accept-Ranges, Content-Length and Content-Type. This extraction does not claim range support.

Native cross-origin audio playback differs from JavaScript fetch/Web Audio in CORS requirements. If the reused player fetches audio or attaches Web Audio, inspect Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Do not infer a need to add crossOrigin.
Captured loader data contains no duration, waveform, encoding, file byte size or response/range headers; none has been invented.

provider_state.guard: useAudioPlayer throws Developer Error if context is absent.
provider_state.persistence: In-memory React state only. Layout me contains an outer AudioPlayerProvider and an inner provider enclosing the main route and player. The inner provider connects radio cards and global player; it can retain state across client route changes while mounted. Reload/remount resets state. The root layout key includes country/locale, so locale-key changes can remount.
provider_state.storage: No localStorage/sessionStorage in the provider or radio route. localStorage calls elsewhere in H6HP6E5F are currentLocale country-selector logic, not player persistence.

radio_route_selection.catalogue: radioTracks.metaobjects.nodes fields are flattened with C(i); a fresh array is reversed for card rendering.
radio_route_selection.on_mount: Effect with [] chooses Math.floor(Math.random()*r.length); only when currentTrack is absent, sets a random track. Does not set isPlaying=true, so initial random selection is not explicit autoplay.
radio_route_selection.different_url_click: setTrack(card); if card.url differs from currentTrack?.url, setPlay(false), then setTimeout(()=>setPlay(true)) with no explicit delay.
radio_route_selection.same_url_click: setTrack(card), then functional toggle of isPlaying.
radio_route_selection.card_icon: Pause icon iff matching selected URL and isPlaying, otherwise play icon.
radio_route_selection.hover_overlay: CSS hides playback overlay on desktop until hover, shows it on narrow layouts. Overlay has pointer-events:none; radio-item-cta handles the click.
radio_route_selection.text_overflow: Mount effect measures each .radio-description-wrapper and adds text-animate to an overwide child span.
radio_route_selection.date_format: MM.DD.YYYY on cards; MM-DD-YYYY in global player.

global_player.native_media: Single <audio ref=d src=currentTrack.url> exists only when a currentTrack exists. No native controls, autoplay attribute, loop attribute or preload setting is declared in JSX.
global_player.play_pause: Effect depending only on [isPlaying] adds a timeupdate listener, then calls audio.play() when true or audio.pause() when false. The UI play/pause button only toggles provider state.
global_player.progress: timeupdate computes currentTime/duration*100 and sets progress. DOM bar width uses that percentage, height10px, #E6E6E6, width0.3s ease-in-out.
global_player.end_behavior: No ended-event listener or next-track action. If computed progress is EXACTLY100, the listener toggles playPause() and resets displayed progress to0. It does not assign audio.currentTime=0.
global_player.seeking: No custom seek handler and no visible native audio controls. Progress bar is display-only in this source.
global_player.volume: No explicit volume/mute state, setter or UI in the inspected source. Playback uses browser/system audio settings.
global_player.next_previous: Absent. No queue, shuffle control or auto-advance at track end; random selection is mount-only when no track exists.
global_player.collapse: resizePlayer toggles full-size flag and .open class. Collapse changes layout; it does not pause audio or clear track.
global_player.route_visibility: Player wrapper visibility is visible when pathname.search matches /radio, products, /policies, /contact, /shop, /looks or /account/login. Otherwise CSS visibility:hidden is used; player/audio is not conditionally unmounted by this route check, so hiding it alone does not stop playback.
global_player.overflow_caption: On isPlaying changes, measures .track-description-copy and adds text-animate when child span is wider.
global_player.media_session: No navigator.mediaSession, MediaMetadata or media-session action handlers in any of the three inspected files.

source_limitations_not_fixed: timeupdate listeners are added on every isPlaying effect without any cleanup, so handlers can accumulate and cause repeated end toggles.
Effect dependency is only isPlaying, not currentTrack; track-switch handler deliberately drives false→timeout→true to invoke playback for new URL.
audio.play() return Promise is not caught; blocked playback can leave React isPlaying=true while native media remains paused.
End detection uses floating percentage equality100 rather than native ended and does not advance tracks.
No finite/zero duration guard around percentage calculation.
Initial random selection assumes non-empty catalogue; an empty array would yield undefined.
No timer cleanup for pending setPlay(true) on route unmount appears in the radio component.
